messages.subject: Re: [SEM] bootstrap in mlr
parts:
Presumably you're getting an error/warning?

MLR is used to estimate standard errors under non-normality. 

Bootstrap is used to estimate standard errors using the parameter estimates. The parameter estimates for MLR are the same as ML, so there's no point bootstrapping MLR estimates.

(How do you know your latent variable is not normal?)

Jeremy





On Mon Dec 29 2014 at 12:56:30 PM Chooza Moon <1982...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi there!

I would like to bootstrap in my SEM model using MLR estimator, because my latent variable is not normally distributed.

I was using the syntax below.

fit <- sem(Mymodel,data=mydata,estimator="mlr", se="bootstrap", test="scaled.shifted", verbose=TRUE)
summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE)

Could anyone give some suggestions?

Thanks a lot!

Best,
Chooza
